title: KV prefetch stability thresholds and sequence-strata calibration for long-context onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable onboarding workflow that produces stable KV-prefetch profiles for models that commonly see long-context workloads (>8k tokens). Current onboarding runs produce noisy prefetch signals for tail sequences which causes oscillation in version selection and suboptimal warmup. This ticket proposes: (1) a stability threshold metric (stability_score) for sequence strata, (2) calibrated prefetch window sizing per stratum, and (3) a canary rollout that locks model-version routing when stability >= threshold for N cycles.

Goals:
- Reduce KV-profile churn for long-context models by at least 40% (measured as version-switch frequency per model per 7d window).
- Keep 99th-pct latency regression vs baseline within 5% after prefetch changes for canaried customers.
- Provide clear telemetry and an automated recommendation for whether to pin a version or keep adaptive routing.

Design decisions & rationale:
- Sequence strata: cluster sequences by token-count bucket + prefix entropy estimate + request origin (API route). This produces strata with similar cache residency behavior and reduces cross-noise between short and long sequences.
- Stability_score: weighted combination of (a) mean cached hit-rate delta between onboarding runs, (b) observed latency variance per stratum, and (c) version-fallback frequency. Weighting favors hit-rate consistency because that most directly impacts cost and cold-latency. Threshold set initially to 0.85.
- Prefetch window calibration: for each stratum compute the smallest prefetch window W such that tail miss-rate drops below 2x baseline miss-rate for the same model with simple fixed W. This minimizes unnecessary KV churn while preserving tail coverage.
- Canary lock: when stability_score >= threshold for 3 consecutive onboarding cycles, emit a routing recommendation and optionally apply a soft lock (metrics-only) followed by a hard lock (version pin) if downstream metrics are stable. Locks are reversible and time-limited.

Trade-offs:
- Higher stability threshold reduces false-positive pins but slows adoption of beneficial new versions. We prefer conservative pins for customers with high SLA needs.
- Per-stratum calibration adds compute to onboarding pipeline; mitigated by sampling only 10% of sequences for expensive simulations and caching intermediate results.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data: assemble a 30-day sampled trace per model keyed by sequence-length, api-route, and prefix-hash. Add fast checksum to detect sequence drift. (owner: data infra)
2) Strata engine: implement lightweight clustering logic in onboarding pipeline to emit strata IDs. (owner: runtime-infra)
3) Stability metric: compute stability_score across runs and store as time-series in TSDB. (owner: telemetry)
4) Prefetch calibrator: run deterministic simulation for each stratum, then choose W. Output candidate prefetch profile artifact (JSON). (owner: onboarding-service)
5) Canary: add rollout hook that can apply soft/hard locks and annotate affected routing policy. (owner: routing)
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline produces per-model, per-stratum prefetch profile artifacts for at least 5 benchmark models
Stability_score calculation and TSDB retention (90 days) implemented and test-covered
Canary lock mechanism implemented (soft and hard) and can be triggered via console and API
End-to-end test: for a selected model, version-switch frequency reduces by >=40% across a 7-day simulated replay
Dashboard panel added to Console showing stability_score, prefetch window, and version-lock state per model
